purpose: Assess ASVS V8 Authorization, the first chapter where the platform's controls are stronger than average - which makes overclaiming, not underclaiming, the risk to guard against.
requiredInvariants: Row level security restricts rows. It is never offered as evidence for a field-level requirement.
Every PASS is bound to named files and re-verified on every run.
A control nothing invokes is not a control; NO_RUNTIME_CALLER makes that checkable.
FAIL is recorded and reported, never resolved by editing product logic.
No product logic, dependency, production, REG.RU, DNS or database change.
acceptance: V8.2.3 is FAIL and its note states explicitly why the row-level control does not answer a field-level requirement.
V8.4.1 and V8.3.1 rest on conditions naming both the transaction wrapper and the policy files.
V8.3.2 rests on the absence of authorization claims in the access token, not on an assertion of immediacy.
V8.3.3 credits the implemented refusal to act on a client's behalf, not merely the absence of impersonation.
All 13 V8 requirements are decided: 7 PASS, 6 FAIL.
The concurrent-scope guard accepts exactly the two authorized paths.
